summary.text: In March 2026 confirmation-hearing remarks, Arvind Raman said that if confirmed he would help NIST deliver on the President's AI action plan and maximize innovation across the American AI tech stack. At the same hearing, he described NIST's AI role as providing measurement science and frameworks for other agencies and said he was committed to the AI action plan. In an August 2026 official statement as NIST Director, he said NIST's contribution to the Genesis Mission reflected its commitment to U.S. leadership in critical technologies and that NIST was using public-private partnerships to apply advanced AI to manufacturing and cybersecurity.

statements.text: Again, as I said in my remarks, the entire AI tech stack advancing America's leadership in chips, both in manufacturing and at the critical edge of next generation chips, will be a high priority for us. And I intend to work with this committee and Congress to make sure, whatever resources you provide that we use it most effectively to make that happen.

attribution.speaker: Arvind Raman

statements.text: Senator, thank you for that question. As I said in my opening remarks, I'm fully committed to helping this deliver on the President's AI action plan. As far as NIST swimlane in this is concerned, it has a very specific expertise and swimlane, and that is to be the gold standard of the measurement science behind AI. And the AI action plan clearly lays out that all NIST should do is really focus on that and then focus on providing frameworks that other agencies can use according to their mission relevance and what they wish to do out of it.

attribution.speaker: Arvind Raman
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Senator, without knowing the details, I'm really not in a position to answer this question. Like I said, in my role, if confirmed as NIST Director, I'll be focusing on the AI action plan and the role that NIST has, you know, stated in it.

statements.text: Thank you for that question, Senator. NIST, of course, has a historic and unique role in AI metrology. Actually, it begins in the 1960s with fingerprinting identification systems. So it's got a really, you know, extensive scientific technical expertise in this. What I will say is that, as I said, I'm fully committed to the AI action plan that the President has laid out.
